summary: SSE stream loses closing line and repeats leading tokens after reverse-proxy injects Content-Length during client path migration
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that SSE responses intermittently arrive with the final line missing while the beginning of the next response is duplicated. Events occur after a mobile client changes networks (NAT mapping change) and the client's corporate reverse proxy is in the path. The customer is on a self-serve account.

Impact:
- Several single-user interactive sessions (chat UI) exhibit missing closing sentences and duplicated leading tokens; affects user experience and downstream parsing.
- Behavior observed across ~8% of reconnects for this customer in the past 24 hours.

Environment:
- Customer-side: Nginx reverse proxy (company-managed) configured with request buffering and a custom header rewrite plugin that adds Content-Length for proxied responses. Client is a mobile web app on iOS with cellular->wifi path migration.
- Redwood: hosted API (prod, us-east-1), API Gateway fronting SSE endpoints, streaming runtime instances serving redwood-gpt-3b and -7b.

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) Open chat in mobile web client behind corporate Nginx.
2) Trigger a long streaming response (~1200 tokens).
3) Switch from cellular to wifi during the stream (path migration / NAT change).
4) Client reconnects; new SSE session is established and stream resumes.
5) Observe duplicated prefix text and absence of the final concluding line in ~1/12 attempts.

Observed logs / artifacts provided by customer:
- Client-side SSE chunks (trimmed):
  [chunk 1] "...the system will return the following configuration:
- enable..."
  [chunk N] "...ensure rotation is scheduled."
  [reconnect chunk] "...the system will return the following configuration:
- enable..."
  [missing final line expected: "In production, monitor X."]
- Customer-provided proxy config snippet: they are forcibly setting Content-Length on proxied responses and enabling proxy_buffering on.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:18 - Customer (support@byteledger.com): 'We're seeing streams cut off — last sentence gone — whenever users flip networks behind our edge proxy. Sometimes the start of the next message repeats. Attached proxy config and a HAR.'

2026-03-12 10:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): 'Thanks — we received your HAR and proxy snippet. Opening investigation. Can you confirm whether the proxy is adding Content-Length on responses that were originally chunked (Transfer-Encoding: chunked)?'
2026-03-12 10:37 - Customer: 'Yes, our plugin normalizes responses and sets Content-Length after buffering.'

2026-03-12 14:22 - Engineering triage (Marco Rivera): 'Reproduced partially in lab with Nginx config that sets Content-Length. Observed early connection close on backend side when proxy believes response complete. Creating capture on gateway and streaming runtime.'

2026-03-13 08:40 - SRE (Diego Kim): 'Gateway trace shows client connection migration followed by upstream proxy issuing FIN while buffered Content-Length smaller than actual stream due to resume fragments. Upstream close triggers SSE session finalization early; runtime still emits trailing tokens which are cut. Also saw identical prefix replay from client side re-init sequence in the new session.'
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Proxy sets Content-Length after buffering initial parts of the stream, and when client path migrates the proxy's buffer is flushed/closed prematurely causing an upstream FIN; gateway interprets as stream termination and does not forward late runtime tokens to the resumed session.

Hypothesis B: Client reconnect includes a re-submitted initial prefix token set; server-side idempotency mapping results in duplicate prefix emission because resumed session is not deduplicating the client's re-sent prompt fragment.

Reproduction: Lab setup with Nginx (proxy_buffering=on; plugin that sets Content-Length) + mobile path migration emulated via iptables NAT change. Reproduced missing final line on 3/10 attempts and duplicated prefix on 2/10 attempts.

Traces and artifacts: Gateway pcap and runtime logs uploaded to internal S3: s3://redwood-internal/support/SUP-306718/traces (link placeholder). Runtime log shows last few token emits after FIN from upstream; gateway logs show HTTP/1.1 200 with Content-Length header followed by unexpected FIN before full stream tokens emitted.

Temporary mitigation test: Turning off proxy's Content-Length injection eliminated missing-final-line in lab. Disabling proxy_buffering reduced but did not eliminate duplicates (suggests two contributing factors).
Related: SUP-314158 contains discussion about window-update and offset shifts on resume; may provide useful heuristics for resume dedupe logic.
resolution:
Workaround and next steps:
1) Customer workaround: Disable the plugin that injects Content-Length on proxied chunked responses or turn off proxy_buffering for streaming endpoints. Customer confirmed they can try a config change and will report results.
2) Short-term platform mitigation: Engineering to add conservative guard in gateway that treats unexpected upstream FIN during streaming as 'soft-close' and attempts to buffer remaining tokens for a configurable grace window before declaring stream finished.
3) Mid-term: Add resume deduplication on the runtime/gateway for client-provided prefix resequences to avoid duplicated leading tokens on rejoin.
4) Postmortem action items: update runbook with detection steps for Content-Length injection and provide a config snippet for Nginx to safely proxy SSE (recommend proxy_buffering off or chunked passthrough).
next_steps: Engineering: implement gateway soft-close grace window (owner: Marco Rivera) — target: 2026-03-20
Engineering: design resume dedupe logic and add unit tests for proxy-induced partial-flush cases (owner: SRE team) — spec due 2026-03-17
Customer: test disabling Content-Length plugin and report results in this ticket (contact: support@byteledger.com)
